title: Mostachones a la Italiana (Italian-Style Mostachones)
description: Prepared with brown sugar, almonds, and candied lemon.

ingredients.name: nutmeg, pepper, and clove to taste
ingredients.sourceText: nutmeg, pepper, and clove to taste

ingredients.name: brown sugar for the glaze
ingredients.sourceText: three pounds brown sugar for the glaze

ingredients.name: one and one-half ounces cinnamon for the glaze
ingredients.sourceText: one and one-half ounces cinnamon for the glaze

steps: Grind three pounds of brown sugar, two pounds of almonds with skin, one and one-half ounces of cinnamon, nutmeg, pepper, and clove to taste according to how spiced you want the mostachones.
After grinding these ingredients well, mix with four pounds of flour and sift through a sieve.
Knead with cold water in a suitable pot, adding a little candied lemon peel while kneading.
After the dough is well worked and manageable, place it on a flour-dusted plate and let it rest two or three hours.

Cut out three or four mostachones to test in the oven to check if it has the right consistency, which you know when they puff up slightly with heat; if they spread instead, add more flour to the dough and knead again.
When ready, cut the mostachones in an oval shape, pointed at the ends, four or five fingers long and three fingers wide.
Bake in the oven; after baking, remove and glaze as follows.

For the glaze: mix three pounds of brown sugar with one and one-half ounces of cinnamon, pass through a sieve, add a little fragrant water, and make it so that when dropped from a spoon it forms a thread.
Brush the glaze onto the mostachones with a brush using this bath.
Place on paper on a table and cover with the hot oven door cover so it sets; when set, store in a humid and cool place, as they are naturally hard.
They can also be glazed with chocolate dissolved in water and made very thick.

title: Mostachones a la Mexicana (Mexican-Style Mostachones)
description: Prepared with syrup, honey, and almonds.

ingredients.name: raw almonds with skin
ingredients.sourceText: one pound of raw almonds with skin

steps: Mix the syrup and virgin honey together and let boil until it reaches the soft-ball stage
Add the raw almonds with skin, hard biscuits, clove and cinnamon, all ground
Add the egg yolks and butter
Place on the heat and stir until it pulls away from the pan
Let cool and form into small figures and dust with cinnamon
If glazed is desired, make a white icing with beaten egg whites, plenty of ground sugar, and a few drops of lemon
Coat the figures on one side with the icing, and when set, turn over and coat the other side
Place on a comal or in a warm oven

title: Mostachones Basados (Glazed Mostachones)
description: Prepared with almond, biscuit, and egg whites.

ingredients.name: two and one-quarter pounds of sugar
ingredients.sourceText: two and one-quarter pounds of sugar

ingredients.name: cleaned almond, pounded
ingredients.sourceText: one pound of cleaned almond, pounded

ingredients.name: ten egg whites and four egg yolks
ingredients.sourceText: ten egg whites and four egg yolks

ingredients.name: cinnamon, clove, and a little pepper, all ground
ingredients.sourceText: cinnamon, clove, and a little pepper, all ground

ingredients.name: finely ground sugar
ingredients.sourceText: one pound of finely ground sugar

steps: Make a well-clarified syrup with two and one-quarter pounds of sugar, removing from heat when it reaches the thread stage
Add one pound of cleaned, pounded almond and give it three boils, removing from heat again
Mix in {{source-2}}
Add gradually ten egg whites and four egg yolks, stirring the dough by hand to prevent lumps from forming
Return to heat and add cinnamon, clove, a little pepper all ground, orange flower water, and {{source-6}}
Cook the dough until it is neither tough nor dry
Dust a board with flour and empty the dough onto it to cool
Cut the mostachones in the style of small hams
Dust with flour so they do not stick and leave on the board until the next day
The next day, beat five egg whites and mix very well with {{source-8}}
Heat this beaten mixture briefly on the heat, add a few drops of lemon, and beat perfectly
Using feathers, coat the mostachones on three sides with this icing
Place on a shovel and put in the oven, which should be gentle, removing as soon as they dry
Coat the remaining three unbathed sides and return to the oven to finish drying so they can be stored

title: Mostachones de Almendra y Limón (Almond and Lemon Mostachones)
description: Prepared with almond, lemon, and orange flower water.
steps: Peel {{source-0}} in hot water and grind it by rolling with water so it does not become oily
Mix away from the heat with clarified syrup at the soft-ball stage made with {{source-1}}
Add half a pound of preserved lemon, removed from its syrup, drained and ground, and {{source-3}}
Return the mixture to the heat and when it has such consistency that it does not stick to the hands, remove again
Empty onto a plate to cool
Form the mostachones into whatever shape is desired and place on papers
Glaze by beating sifted sugar, cinnamon powder, and orange flower water until the mixture forms threads when lifted
Coat the mostachones with a brush
Cover with a comal with a little heat to dry them
When cold, store in a humid place so they do not harden if they are not to be served immediately

title: Mostachones de Almendra y Naranja (Almond and Orange Pastries)
description: A pastry dish made with orange, ground almonds, and sugar.

ingredients.name: soaked and well-ground almonds
ingredients.sourceText: one pound of soaked and well-ground almonds

ingredients.name: half pound of orange preserve (candied orange, drained from syrup and ground)
ingredients.sourceText: half pound of orange preserve (candied orange, drained from syrup and ground)

ingredients.name: three quarters ounce of ground cinnamon
ingredients.sourceText: three quarters ounce of ground cinnamon

ingredients.name: a small amount of grated nutmeg
ingredients.sourceText: a small amount of grated nutmeg

steps: Mix together the sifted sugar, fine flour, ground almonds, candied orange, ground cinnamon, and grated nutmeg
Knead everything by rolling with water until the dough becomes manageable
Place the dough on a plate dusted with flour and let it rest for two hours

After two hours, test the dough by making one pastry and baking it in a well-tempered oven to see if it is ready; if it puffs up, the dough is good, and you may make the remaining pastries in whatever shape you desire
If the test pastry spreads, it is a sign the dough lacks flour, so add more flour
Once the pastries are made, glaze them as described in the previous article

title: Muéganos (Honey Fritters)
description: Prepared with lard, egg yolks, and flour.
steps: Add {{source-1}} to the flour in a pan
Dissolve two egg yolks and incorporate the flour, mixing in the lard
Dissolve the amount of tequesquite that fits between four fingers in a cup of hot water
Once the dough is kneaded, add this to the dough and knead again like washing clothes
Make long, thin rolls the thickness of a finger
Cut into small pieces with a knife
Bake two panels in the oven
Throw them in a cup of water
Put on the heat and when they break apart and the boiling starts, remove from heat
Add the little balls and form the muéganos

description: Prepared with panela, honey, and egg yolks.

ingredients.sourceText: half an eggshell of water of tequesquite

steps: Clarify {{source-0}}, one panela, and half a gill of virgin honey together
Strain and return to heat until it reaches soft-ball stage when tested in water
Mix {{source-3}} with thirty egg yolks without any whites
Add one eggshell of Jerez wine, one of anise water, and half an eggshell of tequesquite water, plus a pinch of salt
Mix everything with the hands and test a small piece in hot lard to see if it puffs; if not, add more of everything except eggs
Form into small sticks, not very thick nor very thin
Leave to air dry, then fry in lard
Once all are fried, place in hot syrup and stir until well coated
Remove and place on a damp board, sprinkle with sesame seeds and empty the pot contents there
Press with a spoon to the desired height and cut as desired
While coating, sprinkle with water

title: Muéganos Poblanos (Fried Pastry Twists from Puebla)
description: A pastry dish made with egg yolks, lard, and wine.

ingredients.name: half a small cup of tequesquite water, settled
ingredients.sourceText: half a small cup of tequesquite water, settled

ingredients.name: one and a half pounds of piloncillo
ingredients.sourceText: one and a half pounds of piloncillo

steps: In a cazuela, combine {{source-0}} and thirty egg yolks, mixing with three fingers of aniseed powder, half a small cup of tequesquite water that has settled, and {{source-4}}.
Knead the mixture, and if it remains loose, add flour until it no longer sticks to the hand.
Beat the dough vigorously on a metate and form long thin sticks that are twisted in the hand.
Fry the sticks in lard (the sticks are made on a table).
Make a syrup with {{source-6}} and one and a half pounds of piloncillo, bringing it to a high glossy point and beating until it crystallizes.
Sprinkle the sticks with Jerez wine, place them in the crystallized syrup, arrange in small boxes, and press them down with a damp napkin on top to smooth them.
Cut into quarter-pound pieces before they harden, without removing them from the box.

title: Nogada para Chiles Rellenos (Walnut Sauce for Stuffed Chiles)
description: A sauce made with chiles, walnuts, and garlic.
steps: Carefully split fifty chiles and soak them in water
Peel and clean them well and place in a pot with clean water
Grind one cup of cleaned walnuts in the metate until very finely ground
Peel garlic cloves and fry them in lard
Once well fried, remove and toast them
In the same lard, fry a little finely minced onion and add the ground walnuts to fry well
Add broth in which the chile meat was cooked, without including the sediment
Fry the broth briefly and add water to cover the chiles
Add soaked and ground bread, a little cinnamon, clove and pepper (all ground), a little thyme and parsley
May also add sliced apple and peach
Add a lump of sugar and a little Sherry wine

title: Nueces en Aguardiente (Walnuts in Brandy)
description: Prepared with walnuts, brandy, and syrup.

ingredients.name: clarified syrup made with two pounds of sugar for every three pounds of walnuts
ingredients.sourceText: clarified syrup made with two pounds of sugar for every three pounds of walnuts

steps: Peel the tender walnuts and place them in cold water as you remove the shell
Place them in water that is close to boiling and let them blanch slightly
Finally place them in boiling water in which a little powdered alum has been dissolved, letting them boil until they are easily pierced with a pin
Remove and place in cold lemon water

Prepare clarified syrup made with two pounds of sugar for every three pounds of walnuts, cooked to the soft-crack stage, and pour over the drained walnuts in a large earthenware bowl, leaving them overnight
The next day, recook the syrup to the hard-crack stage and pour again over the walnuts in the bowl, leaving them for a full day
On the third day, cook the syrup to the low pearl stage and pour over the walnuts
On the fourth and final day, cook the syrup until it reaches the high pearl stage and pour over the walnuts, then mix with equal quantities of refined Spanish brandy
Heat everything so it crackles without boiling, and after cooling slightly, bottle, making sure the walnuts are well coated

title: Nuez Moscada (Agua Espirituosa de) (Spirituous Water of Nutmeg)
description: Prepared with nutmeg, water, and brandy.
steps: Scrape rather than grind the nutmeg
Distill in fourteen cuartillos of refined Spanish brandy with a little water over moderate heat, continuing until the phlegm or tails begin to fall
For common quality: make syrup with one and a half pounds of sugar and ten cuartillos of water
For double quality: make syrup with eight cuartillos of water and two pounds of sugar
For fine and dry quality: make syrup with twelve to sixteen cuartillos of brandy and eight cuartillos of water with one and a half pounds of sugar
Mix the spirit with the syrup, filter in the customary manner
Once clear, the operation is complete

title: Obleas con Aceite para Barquillos (Oil Wafers for Wafer Tubes)
description: Prepared with brandy, olive oil, and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: half a quarter quart of flour
ingredients.sourceText: half a quarter quart of flour

steps: Place half a quarter quart of flour in a bowl and make a hole in the middle, pouring into it two tomas of fine salt, one spoonful of brandy, one spoonful of olive oil and three eggs
Dissolve the flour by pouring it toward the middle without disturbing the edges, being necessary that the whole forms only a single lump
Gradually moisten with good milk until the dough becomes like a thin pap
Heat the wafer iron over a fire that makes no smoke
When it is heated without turning red, grease its interior with a brush dipped in oil
Pour the batter with a measuring spoon and heat the wafer iron for two minutes on each side
The wafers should turn out yellow and of equal color and detach from the mold by themselves, and when removed sprinkle them with ground sugar
Although the first one may be ruined, a little practice will teach the appropriate degree of heat

title: Obleas de Crema para Barquillos (Cream Wafers for Cornets)
description: Prepared with cream, powdered sugar, and orange.

ingredients.name: half an ounce of orange blossom water
ingredients.sourceText: half an ounce of orange blossom water

steps: Beat fourteen ounces of flour with six ounces of fresh cream, and when it no longer forms lumps, add {{source-2}}
Mix everything and add half an ounce of orange blossom water, beating so that the mixture becomes as liquid as cooked milk
Heat the wafer iron and grease it with a brush dipped in fresh butter, melted in an earthenware pot
Pour one and a half spoonfuls of the batter into the mold to form the wafer and press the wafer iron slightly to make it thinner
Place the instrument over charcoal fire on a stove, turning it to the other side when the wafer is cooked on the first side
To know its degree of cooking, half-open the wafer iron, and if the wafer has taken on a good color, open it completely
Remove the wafer with the help of a knife passed underneath, rolling or wrapping itself as it is peeled off
Still hot, shape it as needed and immediately put it in a drying oven so it remains well dried

ingredients.name: two small glasses of good brandy
ingredients.sourceText: two small glasses of good brandy

steps: Place one quarter quart of flour in a bowl and separate a quarter of it to make a light yeast with two drachms of beer foam and a little warm water
Let the yeast ferment at the bottom of the bowl, and once well fermented, add two drachms or a quarter ounce of salt, {{source-4}}, {{source-5}} and six eggs
Mix everything well at once and finish this operation by moistening with hot cream, being necessary that the dough becomes as liquid as frying batter
Cover the bowl and let it ferment for two hours in a warm place, adding two small glasses of good brandy when an hour and a half has passed
Then knead thoroughly so it breaks or becomes corrupted and then heat the wafer iron to cook the wafers at serving time, which is done by bringing them to the table with powdered sugar on top

sourceSteps: Place one quarter quart of flour in a bowl and separate a quarter of it to make a light yeast with two drachms of beer foam and a little warm water
Let the yeast ferment at the bottom of the bowl, and once well fermented, add two drachms or a quarter ounce of salt, one ounce of sugar, four ounces of butter and six eggs
Mix everything well at once and finish this operation by moistening with hot cream, being necessary that the dough becomes as liquid as frying batter
Cover the bowl and let it ferment for two hours in a warm place, adding two small glasses of good brandy when an hour and a half has passed
Then knead thoroughly so it breaks or becomes corrupted and then heat the wafer iron to cook the wafers at serving time, which is done by bringing them to the table with powdered sugar on top

title: Olla Cubana (Cuban Stew)
description: Prepared with veal, ham, and chickpeas.
steps: Prepare a medium pot with water to the middle.
Add a little salt, 2 pounds of veal from the kidneys, a piece of ham, a handful of soaked chickpeas, and 1 pound of fresh pork.
Add a quarter chicken and place to cook, being careful to remove the foam.

After it has boiled for about an hour, add well peeled and cleaned: a banana with its peel, a chorizo, a handful of green beans, half cabbage, a piece of squash, an eggplant, a little malanga, a piece of Castilian squash, two turnips, two sweet potatoes, four tomatoes, two chayotes, an onion and a piece of squash.

Let everything boil for another hour, being careful to remove any foam that rises, and for seasoning grind a little salt, two or three garlic cloves, some cumin grains and cilantro with two of pepper, and once everything is made into a paste, dissolve with broth from the pot, and add to it with two threads of crumbled saffron.
Let it boil a while and serve.

title: Olla ó Cocido Veracruzano (Veracruz Stew)
description: Prepared with veal, beef, and bacon.
steps: Take a pot containing about 2 jarros of cold water.
Place in it 2 pounds of veal, 2 pounds of beef and a piece of Veracruz bacon.
Place over low heat, adding 2 more jarros of water once the first ones have lost their coldness.
Increase the heat to produce foam; remove it as it rises until no more appears.

After boiling for about eight hours over equal heat, when it has been cooking for four hours, add half cabbage, a lettuce, two or three turnips, equal quantity of carrots, a handful of soaked chickpeas, giblets of a turkey, half a chicken and some roasted lamb bones, a little parsley, three cloves and a roasted onion, and add hot water if needed, until the eight hours mentioned are complete.

title: Olla-Podrida a la Francesa en Imitación de la Española (French-Style Olla-Podrida in Imitation of the Spanish)
description: Prepared with beef, veal, and ham.

ingredients.name: a proportionate quantity of desalted ham
ingredients.sourceText: a proportionate quantity of desalted ham

ingredients.name: eight sausages with red chile inside
ingredients.sourceText: eight sausages with red chile inside

steps: Prepare and tie {{source-0}} with twine
Prepare one sheep breast, one veal tendon, and a proportionate quantity of desalted ham
Prepare two old partridges cut like stuffed chicken, one duck, one hen, and two squabs
Soak {{source-11}} in warm water since the day before
Arrange all prepared meats in a braising vessel with the soaked chickpeas
Moisten everything with great broth and bring to a boil
Add six very hot chiles, four cloves of spice, a little nutmeg, and a little mace wrapped in clean cloth
Allow everything to continue boiling until completely cooked, removing the most tender chickpeas
Prepare four cabbages, ten lettuces, thirty carrots, and thirty turnips, shaping them with the greatest evenness possible
Parboil everything and arrange in a covered saucepan with slices of ham
Moisten with the defatted broth from the braising vessel
Prepare one dozen artichoke hearts, trimmed and rounded, cooking them in white broth with twenty-four blanched onions
Shape carrots and turnips in the form of olives and cook them in concentrated broth with a little sugar
Prepare green beans, green beans, cucumbers or gherkins, and peas, parboiling each article and setting each aside
Strain the broth from the braising vessel, degrease it, clarify it, strain again through a cloth, and keep it boiling

Squeeze the cabbages and lettuces and arrange them on a large platter in the following order: a piece of cabbage, a carrot, a lettuce, and a turnip, covering the circumference of the platter in a circle, placing the chickpeas in the spaces
Arrange the meats in order in the middle of the platter and the twelve artichoke hearts on the border of the vegetables at equal distance, placing the blanched onions between them
Heat the small vegetables well, sauté them with gelatin and butter, and arrange them like bouquets in the artichoke hearts
Finally cover all the meats with gelatin
Serve everything very hot with the concentrated broth served separately

title: Olla-Podrida en Seco (Dry Olla-Podrida)
description: Prepared with rice, lamb, and chickpeas.
steps: One day before serving, wash rice early in the morning, changing the water several times and let it soak for about an hour
Drain it well and place it in the sun to dry on a napkin
In cold water, soak lamb and chickpeas
In separate water, soak fat cured beef or pork, pieces of ham, one or two pig tails, a piece of bacon, three or four chorizos, sausages and pieces of longaniza
In the afternoon, wash and remove fat from the lamb, divide it into regular portions
Divide one or two chickens into quarters
Clean the ham or bacon with hot water
Prepare vegetables of all kinds, wash them well and let everything drain
Cover the bottom of a proportioned pot with tender cabbage leaves
On them place a layer of desalted fat cured meat, and on that another layer of thick slices of cabbage, lettuce and chard, well cleaned

Add four to six whole garlic heads, the same number of onion heads, four to six wide chiles, an equal number of cleaned turnips and carrots, with a good portion of chickpeas and rice that have been soaking
On this layer place another of lamb portions and chicken quarters, pieces of bacon and ham
Form another layer with all the substances that were put with the cabbage and other vegetables, repeating on top the lamb, chicken and ham
Cover this with vegetables, and the last layer is formed with all the pork meats, such as tails, bacon, cured meat, chorizos, sausages and longaniza

Once the pot is arranged this way, grind cumin, clove, cinnamon, ginger, saffron, black pepper and sea salt in proportionate quantity and dissolve in a cup of water, which is poured into the pot without adding more water
Cover with a dish that fits well to the mouth, and seal the joints around with starch paste
In the evening of the day before the olla is to be used, place it on a very low fire covered with hot ashes, and maintain it on that fire until midday the following day, trying to keep the fire even
To prevent burning, put a little water in the dish covering the pot, without allowing this water to dampen the paste sealing it

Some, after arranging all the layers in the olla-podrida, dissolve the spices in a quarter-liter of white wine and another quarter-liter of Castilian vinegar, distributing the resulting broth in the vegetable layers, then covering the pot as described

When about to serve, mix with three egg yolks dissolved in cream.

title: Ostiones en sus Conchas (Oysters in their Shells)
description: Prepared with oysters, onions, and broth.
steps: Open four dozen oysters, remove them from their shells, and give them a boil in the same water they have released.
Remove from heat and place a little butter in a pan with very tender chopped onions and parsley.
Sauté and add a tablespoon of flour, dissolving everything with broth and half a glass of white wine.
Cook and reduce this sauce by adding the oysters to it.
Set aside the largest and cleanest shells and after washing well, place three or four oysters with appropriate sauce in each, covering with breadcrumbs and a little butter.
At the moment of serving, place on grills covered with a griddle full of coals and leave for a few minutes.

title: Otra Veracruzana (Another Veracruz-Style Beef)
description: Prepared with meat, ham, and garlic.

ingredients.name: eighteen to twenty heads of garlic
ingredients.sourceText: eighteen to twenty heads of garlic

steps: Cut solid meat into large pieces and remove the skin.
Soak in cold water to bleed, then wash and slice.
Clean with cloth so it has no blood.
Grind cloves, pepper, cinnamon, and a little salt.
Cut ham into strips and peel garlic cloves.
Mix thyme with everything.
Stud the meat pieces with ham mixed together, ground spices, and garlic.

Tie the meat pieces with strong thread and put in a pot with sufficient water, one bottle of Mexican vinegar and a little Castilian vinegar, eighteen to twenty heads of garlic, a handful of Castilian pepper, a little bay leaf, thyme with stalks, and salt.
Heat, cover the pot and stir from time to time so the meat does not stick.
When cooked, remove and let cool.
Once cold, remove the thread, cut into slices the thickness of a finger, and put in a dish with Mexican vinegar and a little Castilian vinegar and one bottle of oil.
Drain the herbs, garlic, and other things from the pot where the meat was cooked.
Add salt to taste and in a small barrel or in the pot place a layer of meat and another of garlic and spices and leave ready to eat.

title: Otras Albóndigas (Other Meatballs)
description: Prepared with pork, veal, and mutton.
steps: Mix pork, veal and mutton meat and remove the skins
Grind clove, cinnamon, pepper, oregano and thyme

Grind on the metate with milk and a piece of bread soaked beforehand in milk and mix with the meat together with the spices, minced ham, raw egg, raisins, almonds, capers, two raw egg yolks and Sherry wine

Put all this in a napkin in the form of a ball and in the middle place a hard-boiled egg studded with strips of ham, tie it in the napkin and put it to cook in salted water and the skins that were removed from the meat
Cover and from time to time poke it with a fork to know when the meat is cooked
Then untie the napkin so the meat cools a little

Brown half a head of garlic that is partly crushed and when well browned add two tablespoons of flour to the lard; when it is browned strain it in the water in which the large meatball was cooked, and add more spices, which are taken from the same ones added to the meat; add half a cup of Sherry wine, two or three bay leaves, parsley leaves, plenty of sliced onion and the large meatball so it finishes cooking
Do not move the large meatball more than with a fork to turn it and let the broth thicken a little

title: Otras Tamales (Other Tamales)
description: Prepared with corn, lard, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: More than three pounds of lard
ingredients.sourceText: More than three pounds of lard

steps: To {{source-0}} add more than three pounds of lard
Prepare the corn as for atole, wash it well and dry with a cloth in the sun
Grind and sift in an ayate
Add a little softened water, beating until it makes like bubbles, and ground sugar
Make the dough thicker because the sugar makes it watery
To know if it is good, make a little ball of dough and put it in water; if it rises it is because it is good
The filling is made of cooked egg yolks, ground sugar, piñones, acitrón, canela and sesame seeds
Place the leaves to drain from the morning so they are not wet
Cook the tamales in a pot like the previous ones and when they sound hollow, detach the leaves they are cooked in
This dough without sugar and without salt can be filled with chile, spices, etc.

title: Otro Pastel de Mantequilla (Another Butter Pastry)
description: A pastry dish made with butter, lard, and flour.
steps: On a very clean surface place half pound of flour; add three eggs, half a tablespoon of lard, a bit of salt and a bit of tequesquite water
Knead everything until it forms eyes and extend with a rolling tool making the dough as thin as possible
Take {{source-5}} that should have been in water to harden and make small balls with it, placing them over half the dough, covering with the other half as if making a quesadilla
Repeat this operation until the size of the quesadilla becomes very small

Extend again with the rolling tool and to prevent it from sticking to the dough, dust flour on another pile of half pound of flour and repeat the same operation with the balls until everything is finished
Extend again with the rolling tool, leaving the dough the thickness of a finger, a little more or less
Cut with molds, and extend the scraps again with the rolling tool without touching them as they will spoil
Bake in the oven, and when they begin to rise, brush with butter and lard using a feather, then dust with sugar powder to form little crusts
When serving, dust more powdered sugar on top

description: Prepared with macaroni, lard, and cheese.

ingredients.name: half a pound of Gruyere cheese
ingredients.sourceText: half a pound of Gruyere cheese

steps: Put the macaroni in a proportionate saucepan with one ounce of lard, salt, pepper and sufficient water to cover it
When the water has been consumed, grate half a pound of Gruyere cheese and add it to the macaroni with one ounce of lard

Line it with a paste two lines thick throughout
Put the macaroni inside, covering it with a layer of the same paste and thickness
Cook over low heat, with heat from above and below, for half an hour
Turn it out onto the plate on which it is to be served

description: Prepared with syrup, flour, and butter.
steps: To two pounds of flour, cook a little anise water and put it back on the heat in a small pan
Add a spoonful of butter and boil until the butter is cooked
Remove from heat and stir in the two pounds of flour until it forms a thick paste and put it back on the heat and cook until it forms a ball and separates from the pan

Then add salt; the butter should be neither hot nor cold so they have room to puff and add syrup

title: Otros Buñuelos de Arroz (Other Rice Fritters)
description: Prepared with rice, lard, and orange.
steps: The day before making the fritters, soak {{source-0}}
The next day, grind it very well, adding a little milk as you grind
In a pan, dissolve one quarter quart of milk, not too thick nor too loose, and two full tablespoons of lard and a grain of salt
Put it on the heat without stopping stirring
When half cooked, add another tablespoon of lard and a little anise
It is well cooked when it is slightly yellow, then remove from heat to cool
Put it on a table to knead it, and add twenty-nine eggs with whites and yolks, adding them little by little
Knead well, giving it many blows
Put a fryer with a wide bottom that covers the heat with {{source-8}}
When well hot, coat the palms of your hands with lard, take a ball of dough and make a hole in the middle with your finger
Fry them in the lard, constantly turning them and striking them from above with a small stick
Clarify {{source-9}} and after straining, put it on the heat and add two orange leaves
When at the proper point, pour it over the fritters

Place to drain on a cloth and arrange on the plate in the form of a crown, pouring the desired sauce in the middle.

title: Panales de Canela Rebanados (Sliced Cinnamon Honeycomb Candy)
description: A confection made with cinnamon, egg whites, and lemon juice.

ingredients.name: White and fluffy sugar, or little compact sugar
ingredients.sourceText: White and fluffy sugar, or little compact sugar

ingredients.name: Water, one cuartillo for each pound of sugar
ingredients.sourceText: Water, one cuartillo for each pound of sugar

ingredients.name: Egg whites for clarifying the syrup
ingredients.sourceText: Egg whites for clarifying the syrup

ingredients.name: Cinnamon powder, one tablespoon per two pozuelos of syrup
ingredients.sourceText: Cinnamon powder, one tablespoon per two pozuelos of syrup

steps: Choose white and fluffy sugar and make syrup with it, calculating one cuartillo of water for each pound of sugar, but setting aside some water both for beating the egg whites to clarify the syrup and to calm the boiling twice
Dissolve the sugar on the fire, stirring with a spoon until completely dissolved
Mix two beaten egg whites in water for each pound of sugar and continue stirring until the sugar is entirely dissolved
Place the pan on high heat so it quickly comes to a boil; when it begins to rise, add some of the separated water to calm it, using this opportunity to remove the foam quickly
When it rises again, add the remaining water and remove the pan from the heat

Outside the fire, skim the syrup again until it is perfectly clean and strain it through a fine cloth, letting what is strained rest until the next day, tilting the pan so the syrup can decant or separate from the sediment

The next day before beginning the operation, prepare two or three small pans or skillets the size of a small plate, the same number of spoons, a small brazier or anafe with fire, a small table with clean napkin, sheets of paper, a bowl or cup with cold water, cut lemons, cinnamon powder and clean popotes

When everything is ready, pour two pozuelos of unskimmed syrup into one of the small pans, placing it on the anafe with moderate heat, and as the syrup begins to boil, skim without inserting the spoon and add sixty drops of lemon

When there is no more foam to remove and the syrup begins to reach its point, test it with the popote, which when inserted in the syrup and then quickly in cold water, the sugar adhering to it should crack between the teeth and break like glass

At this point remove from the fire, beat it, and when it begins to rise, quickly pour it onto the paper, slicing as the fire cools before it hardens, but without separating the slices, which is left for when the honeycomb has cooled well
When this operation is finished, repeat in another pan with another spoon, because there is not time to wash the first one well, and for this reason several are prepared
Decrease the amount of lemon if the honeycomb has too much or add it if it has too little
When beating the two pozuelos of syrup, while one is being worked on, add one tablespoon of cinnamon powder to the other, which is the quantity proportioned to that syrup
In this way the pores of the honeycomb remain very fine and it is solid and of a delicate flavor

title: Panales Quemados (Burnt Sugar Candies)
description: A confection made with sugar, egg whites, and lemon juice.
steps: Clarify the syrup in the common manner, with the only difference that for one pound of sugar add four egg whites, or more if desired, beating them in water with some switches.
Place to cook over good heat, stirring until it has acquired the high point of 'flower' or nearly so, but without skimming.
Strain through a sieve, pour into a pan, and if you want it more toasted, let it cook until on the walls of the pan the sugar appears reddish or yellowish.
Afterwards remove it from the heat, and placing it on a firm surface, add four drops of lemon juice for each pound of sugar.
Beat strongly and without ceasing, until the sugar has puffed up and risen high.
Let it rest again, and with a small saw within the same pan divide it into long pieces of half a quarter and the thickness of an inch or so in square, more or less.
Once everything is divided in this way, put it back on the heat so it becomes detached and so it can be removed without breaking, taking care not to mistreat it.
Being warm equally, turn the vessel carefully onto a paper placed on a table, where the pieces are finished separating.
For this type of sugar candy, brown sugar can be used.

title: Panza de Carnero Rellena (Stuffed Lamb Tripe)
description: Prepared with lamb, tripe, and lemon.
steps: Clean the tripe very well, making sure the hole is not too large
Turn the tripe inside out to remove all impurities
Heat water, pour over the tripe and remove immediately
Scrape with a knife until clean
Take the intestines, turn them inside out after washing, wash inside by squeezing lemon juice in the water and rub well with lemon peel
Cook all together except the tripe with water and salt
When cooked, cut into small pieces
Chop tomato without seeds, six garlic cloves, a bunch of onion and some parsley, all very finely
Put this in a pot with butter, first add the garlic, before it browns add the onion, then the tomato and parsley
Let fry well, then add water and the intestines, ham pieces, whole chorizos, sliced testicles, capers, olives, chiles in vinegar, raisins, almonds and pine nuts
Grind six peppercorns, six cloves, and some saffron threads with salt, add to the pot and boil until completely dry like ground meat, then remove from heat
Take the tripe, fill it through the hole and sew it closed
Place a pot with butter, salt and water on the heat and add the tripe; the water should cover it, turning it so it does not burn
In another pot, cook ground tomatoes without seeds, fry well, and add to the pot with the tripe
Let reduce greatly, add clove, cinnamon, pepper and saffron all ground, thyme, chopped parsley, and some Sherry wine
The sauce should be thick and garnish with lettuce leaves

title: Papas a la Alemana (German-Style Potatoes)
description: Prepared with potatoes, water, and butter.
steps: Clean twelve large potatoes and cut them into very thin slices.
Put them to cook in water over strong heat.
When they appear ready to fall apart in substance, drain them.
Return them to the same pot over the fire, stirring strongly with a wooden spoon.
Add {{source-2}}, salt, pepper, nutmeg and chopped parsley.
Break three eggs into them without ceasing to stir this mixture until it becomes solid.
Let it cool then.
Have melted butter ready in a large sauté pan and put the potatoes into it as if they were thick quenelles.
Make them take color over strong heat and turn them so they brown equally on all sides.

title: Papino de Arroz y Almidón (Rice and Starch Papino)
description: Prepared with rice, starch, and egg yolks.
steps: Wash {{source-0}} in cold water and then in hot water.
Dry it and then grind it.
When ground, weigh it and complete one pound with sifted starch, replacing what the rice has lost.
Mix everything with six quarters of milk, sweetened well with sugar, and having mixed everything in the milk, strain through a sieve without ceasing to stir everywhere.
Once it is boiling, beat ten egg yolks and add them to the milk with a little orange blossom water.
Give it the half-point of manjar blanco and add a little carmine, enough to give it a pink color.
Before sweetening, add two grains of sea salt, and it can be served as ante over layers of mamón.

title: Pasta de Agraz (Verjuice Paste)
description: Prepared with verjuice and pears or apples.
steps: Select verjuice nearly ripe, remove the seeds, and place on the fire to burst, stirring with a spatula
Add some peeled pears or apples divided into pieces
When everything is well dissolved, pass through a fine bristle sieve so that only the skins and pits remain
Place this pulp in a pan on the fire to dry as much as necessary to acquire consistency, then weigh it
Make a syrup with an equal amount of sugar as the weight of the fruit
When the syrup reaches the high blown point, add the pulp and let it boil until it reaches point, stirring constantly with a spatula that must not be removed at all

When the paste detaches perfectly from the bottom of the pan or the pot, it is a sign that it is done and it is then poured into tin molds or paper boxes, which are dried in the stove, dusting them with fine sugar

description: Prepared with almond, cinnamon, and sugar.

ingredients.name: a pound and a half of sugar

ingredients.name: half a pound of soaked and ground almond

ingredients.name: half an ounce of ground cinnamon
ingredients.sourceText: half an ounce of ground cinnamon

steps: Make a clarified syrup at the preserve point with a pound and a half of sugar
Off the fire, mix in half a pound of soaked and ground almond
Return to the fire and stir constantly until the bottom of the pan is visible

If to be served in perforated papers, form the paste into balls, place in the papers, and glue them with gum

title: Pasta para Matas (Choux Paste)
description: Prepared with water, butter, and sugar.
steps: Place in a saucepan one cuartillo of water, one quarter of butter, some small pieces of lemon peel, one quarter of sugar and a little salt
Bring to boil, and before it begins to boil remove from heat and remove the lemon peel, adding flour little by little, as much as the water can absorb
Stir continuously and place on fire for five or six minutes, without stopping stirring
When the paste is ready it will be known because it separates from the pan; then transfer to a glazed bowl, and add eggs one by one until the paste sticks to the fingers
Butter and flour a platter, and place this paste on top in pieces the size of a walnut
Add chopped almonds with ground sugar, and put in the oven; this paste can be made into rolls, giving them whatever shape is desired; it should be baked in a moderate oven

title: Pastel Americano (American Pastry)
description: A pastry dish made with prunes, powdered sugar, and sugar.

ingredients.name: two whole eggs and two yolks only
ingredients.sourceText: two whole eggs and two yolks only

ingredients.name: one small cup of tequesquite water
ingredients.sourceText: one small cup of tequesquite water

steps: Clarify {{source-0}} and once clarified add {{source-1}}
Let it reach a high point, and when at this point remove the pits

Place {{source-2}} on a board, make a mound and in the center put two whole eggs and two yolks only, a pinch of salt, {{source-5}}, one small cup of tequesquite water, and about twelve ounces of butter
Knead everything very well and let it rest a bit
Meanwhile butter a pan
Roll out one third of the dough to the thickness of a thick cigar and the shape of the pan
Cook over two fires and when done place the preserve and cover with another part of the dough that is also rolled out
Place again to brown, and when it is nearly done coat with a small amount of butter
Decorate with the rest of the dough as desired and add the remaining butter (a pound total)
Place again to finish cooking and brown well
Serve hot

title: Pastel Caliente Costra (Hot Pastry Crust)
description: A pastry dish made with dough, flour, and egg.

ingredients.name: optional: rabbit, larks or other meats
ingredients.sourceText: optional: rabbit, larks or other meats

steps: Mold or arrange two pounds of dough into a well rounded form
Flatten evenly with a rolling pin
Fold three inches of dough at the edge between the fingers, avoiding creases or wrinkles
Raise to a convenient height
Make the size of an appetizer plate, garnishing if desired with what will go inside, such as rabbit or larks, or if not, fill the interior of the pastry with flour only
Cover and decorate by brushing with a broken and beaten egg using a feather brush
Put into a preheated oven
Be careful not to brown too much
When cooked, empty by removing the interior dough and replace with a stew
To make a raised crust to cover it, use the same procedures and place its crust cover on the pastry

title: Pastel de Leche (Milk Pie)
description: A pastry dish made with milk, beef marrow, and pine nuts.

ingredients.name: beef marrow bones
ingredients.sourceText: two pounds of beef marrow bones

steps: Grind {{source-0}} with sufficient pine nuts, almonds and hazelnuts, making a paste, adding four dozen eggs
Mix afterwards with one quarter arroba of flour, {{source-6}}, ten more egg yolks and {{source-8}} and knead everything with a little water
Form the pie with this mass, which will be filled with a paste of egg threads made in this way: put {{source-10}} in eight cuartillos of milk, and the yolks of four dozen eggs
After everything is well dissolved, pass it through a threader or skimmer, making it fall into boiling well clarified syrup
Cover the pie with the dough said before, dust on top with panela, sugar and cinnamon, all ground and bake in the oven

title: Pastel de Mantequilla (Butter Pastry)
description: A pastry dish made with butter, lard, and flour.

ingredients.name: little more than one quarter pound of flour
ingredients.sourceText: little more than one quarter pound of flour

steps: Spread on a table a little more than one quarter pound of flour, three whole eggs and a bit of salt, half a tablespoon of lard, a bit of tequesquite water, and work everything together until it forms eyes or blisters
Extend with a rolling tool to regular thickness, and begin placing small balls of butter until they cover half the dough
Fold over the other half as if making ravioli, fold again and roll
Make some holes in the dough and add the rest of the pound of flour, using up the pound of butter
Do not touch the dough with your hand, only with the rolling tool or a knife
Once well kneaded, extend to the thickness of a finger or a little less, cut with a mold and place over low heat
Place in a casserole over the fire, and when they begin to cook, brush the pastries with butter using feather barbs, and cover with powdered sugar
Cover the casserole with a comal until they finish cooking, being careful they do not brown too much
Once cooked, cover again with sugar

title: Pastel de Masa Tierna (Tender Dough Pastry)
description: A pastry dish made with dough, ham, and lard.

ingredients.name: Ham with good lean meat, in thin slices
ingredients.sourceText: Ham with good lean meat, in thin slices

ingredients.name: Half a cuartillo of good vinegar
ingredients.sourceText: Half a cuartillo of good vinegar

ingredients.name: Meat from legs and wings of hens, boned
ingredients.sourceText: Meat from legs and wings of hens, boned

ingredients.name: Orange leaf powder or orange peel
ingredients.sourceText: Orange leaf powder or orange peel

steps: Cut thin slices of ham with good lean meat and fry in lard until cooked
Roast very ripe tomatoes, grind them well, and dissolve in half a cuartillo of good vinegar
Add to the pot where the ham is frying
Add a piece of panocha the size of an egg and a small amount of water with salt
Boil everything until the broth is consumed leaving only the grease
Remove the ham and fry the cooked chicken breasts and chopped miscellaneous poultry pieces and meat from the legs and wings of hens, deboned
Once everything is browned, remove the meat and fry a sauce made of desalted capers and ground egg yolks, adding ground cloves, cinnamon, pepper, and necessary salt
Chop half of the ham slices, all the meat and poultry remnants that were fried, except the breasts
Mix the chopped mixture with the sauce and place in a platter
Arrange the breasts and remaining ham slices on top
Cover the platter with a sheet made of the tender dough explained before
Form thin strips of the same dough and place them around the edge of the platter in four to six layers, one on top of another
Using the thumb, cut them along the edge all around so they rise when cooked and look good
Apply fire from above until the dough browns
When browned, dust with very fine orange leaf or orange peel powder and sifted sugar
Apply fire from above again for two or three minutes to melt it, then remove

title: Pastel de Menudillos de Puerco (Pork Offal Pastry)
description: A pastry dish made with pork, pork liver, and shallots.
steps: Put a good pork liver, cut into slices, in a pan with four ounces of butter and a handful of chopped parsley and shallots
When the liver is half cooked, let it cool for a quarter hour

Cut ham into dice equal in amount to the liver and make a good filling with it, mixing together, seasoning with spices, nutmeg, pepper and salt, and adding what remains in the pan where the liver was fried

title: Pastel de Vino (Wine Cake)
description: A cake made with wine, egg yolks, and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: powdered sugar in sufficient quantity to make the dough somewhat sweet
ingredients.sourceText: powdered sugar in sufficient quantity to make the dough somewhat sweet

ingredients.name: a little melted and cooled butter
ingredients.sourceText: a little melted and cooled butter

ingredients.name: generous wine as much as necessary to moisten the dough
ingredients.sourceText: generous wine as much as necessary to moisten the dough

steps: Make the dough with half a pound of flour heaped on the table with a hole in the middle, into which pour three egg yolks, powdered sugar in sufficient quantity so the dough becomes somewhat sweet, a little melted and cooled butter, and generous wine as much as necessary to moisten the dough, which should remain tender
Knead everything together, and when smooth, extend with a rolling pin so that the dough becomes very thin

Cut some round discs the size of the platter in which the cake is to be served, and arrange three or four of them stacked on top of each other to serve as a base on the same plate after it has been greased with butter, with the dough sheets for the base greased the same way
Add on top a filling composed away from the heat with syrup at high point, generous wine, clove and cinnamon powder, ground ladyfinger biscuit, raisins, almonds, walnuts, pine nuts and toasted sesame
Once this filling is well arranged, stud it with more raisins, walnuts, almonds, pine nuts and candied citron pieces, and cover everything with two or three other very thin sheets of the same dough
Wet the edges so the covering adheres and pinch the edges all around
Decorate on top with small figures of the same dough and brush with butter using feathers
Place in the oven, and when cooked and still hot, dust the upper part with ground powdered sugar and decorate the figures or designs with which it has been adorned with dragée

title: Pasteles de Asador (Roasted Bird Pastries)
description: A pastry dish made with rice flour, egg yolks, and wine.

ingredients.name: Rice flour, about half a pound
ingredients.sourceText: Rice flour, about half a pound

steps: Beat rice flour with eight or ten egg yolks and half a pound of sugar
Moisten with necessary wine to make it spreadable and mix everything well
Take a squab or equal bird, remove the neck and wings cleanly
Coat with salt and finely ground fine spices
Wrap in paper greased with lard and spit-roast over fire until cooked
Remove the paper and let it brown
Coat with the flour and egg mixture, place by the fire
As it dries, alternately apply baths of lard and batters using feathers until the bird is well covered
Give a final bath of lard, and when dry, dust with sifted sugar mixed with cinnamon
Serve

Place in the oven and bake for about one hour
Instead of rabbit, slices of beef or cow meat may be used

description: A pastry dish made with milk, egg yolks, and almonds.
steps: Make the dough with two quarter litres of milk, two pounds of ground sugar, three egg yolks, four pounds of almonds and one handful of pine nuts, all well ground
Heat until the dough takes on a firm consistency so the pastries can be formed
Remove from heat and when it cools a bit, form as before and fill with any paste, preferably the following

Mix in two pounds of white sweet potato that has no fibers
Grate one large coconut
Grind one pound of blanched almonds
Mix everything well and place on the fire
When it begins to reach cajeta consistency, add one cup of vanilla and bring to a high cajeta consistency

title: Pastelón de Mantequilla (Butter Pastry Cake)
description: A cake made with butter, lard, and minced filling.

ingredients.name: good flour, well sifted
ingredients.sourceText: one pound of good flour, well sifted

ingredients.name: pieces of cooked tender ham and chicken
ingredients.sourceText: pieces of cooked tender ham and chicken

steps: Place one pound of good sifted flour on a table and mix with water and salt
Soften the mixture with all the lard necessary to work it
Let it rest covered for a while
Gradually extend it into very thin sheets and coat with melted and cold butter
Roll as thick as desired and flatten with a rolling pin
Cut the dough to the size the pastry cake should be

Butter a serving dish and place as base and filling a minced mixture with pieces of cooked tender ham and chicken in pieces, olives, chili peppers in quarters, capers, large capers, raisins and almonds to a proportionate height
Cover with another layer of dough equal to the bottom, either in one piece or in three or four
Stack pieces overlapping at the sides so that when cooked it forms like a cloud
If desired woven, cut the dough into strips two fingers wide, make a crosshatch pattern, and with another large strip cover at the edge of the dish all the points of the weave
Place in a well-tempered oven so it is not undercooked and flattened, nor burned
When done, sprinkle sifted sugar so it adheres

ingredients.name: sifted sugar, as much as comes out

steps: Make a ring with half a pound of flour on a table
Into the center put 3 egg yolks, sifted sugar, a little melted and cooled lard, and generous wine as needed to moisten
The dough should be tender; extend it with a rolling pin
Cut very thin tortillas the size of the dish in which it will be made
Butter the dish and place 3 or 4 of these tortillas on the bottom, also buttered
For the filling: make a paste away from heat with generous wine syrup, generous wine, clove and cinnamon powder, ground mamón, raisins, almonds, walnuts, pine nuts, and toasted sesame
Season and make it somewhat thick; place on the tortillas
Arrange according to taste, flat or elevated, and stud with more raisins, almonds, walnuts, pine nuts, and pieces of candied pumpkin or citron
Place 2 or 3 more very thin tortillas on top and seal at the edge of the dish
Decorate with figures and designs made of the same dough
Brush with sufficient butter using feathers and put in a well-tempered oven
As soon as it is done, before cooling, sprinkle sifted sugar or small candies on the designs on the upper side
Note: Adding cooked bone marrow to the filling gives it another flavor

title: Pastillas de Azahar (Orange Blossom Lozenges)
description: Prepared with orange and white sugar.

ingredients.name: three or four pounds of superfine white sugar
ingredients.sourceText: three or four pounds of superfine white sugar

ingredients.name: double quantity of orange blossom water
ingredients.sourceText: double quantity of orange blossom water

steps: Pound three or four pounds of superfine white sugar in a marble mortar, separating the finest part for other compositions as described.

Dissolve the remaining sugar in a clean earthenware vessel with double quantity of orange blossom water, using a small spatula while pouring the water gently and at intervals until the paste condenses.
If too much water was added and the paste is liquid, thicken it with a little powdered sugar kept in reserve.
It is ready when a portion taken with the spatula and tilted falls off by itself.
Place four ounces of this paste in a spouted pan on a hot burner and heat the paste until it liquefies, stirring with a flat stick shaped like a spatula.
When the paste begins to boil, remove the pan and stir two or three more times, then pour onto tin sheet plates as follows:

Hold the pan with the left hand and tilt its spout gently, allowing the paste to flow while using a knitting needle attached to a wooden handle held in the right hand to guide it, directing the pan or needle alternately so the paste falls onto the plates in the shape of small buttons about the size of a coin, which are called lozenges.
Endeavor to line them up as they are made and that all have the same quantity of paste, which is only achieved by keeping the left hand steady.
After one hour, remove from the plates and place on papers in the oven, where they should remain one day, as more time would diminish the perfume.
These lozenges can produce twenty pounds or more per day.

sourceIngredients: three or four pounds of superfine white sugar

sourceSteps: Pound three or four pounds of superfine white sugar in a marble mortar, separating the finest part for other compositions as described.

Dissolve the remaining sugar in a clean earthenware vessel with double quantity of orange blossom water, using a small spatula while pouring the water gently and at intervals until the paste condenses.
If too much water was added and the paste is liquid, thicken it with a little powdered sugar kept in reserve.
It is ready when a portion taken with the spatula and tilted falls off by itself.
Place four ounces of this paste in a spouted pan on a hot burner and heat the paste until it liquefies, stirring with a flat stick shaped like a spatula.
When the paste begins to boil, remove the pan and stir two or three more times, then pour onto tin sheet plates as follows:

Hold the pan with the left hand and tilt its spout gently, allowing the paste to flow while using a knitting needle attached to a wooden handle held in the right hand to guide it, directing the pan or needle alternately so the paste falls onto the plates in the shape of small buttons about the size of a coin, which are called lozenges.
Endeavor to line them up as they are made and that all have the same quantity of paste, which is only achieved by keeping the left hand steady.
After one hour, remove from the plates and place on papers in the oven, where they should remain one day, as more time would diminish the perfume.
These lozenges can produce twenty pounds or more per day.
